text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
-The central bank has had little success in halting the appreciation of the crown. On Thursday the currency reached the same level as before the rate cut on Tuesday.

-The new government has decided that Bosnian refugees will not be forced to leave Norway against their will. The opposition welcomed the decision, but said they wanted a solution for refugees who are living under protection of the church as well.

-The Oslo Bourse has decided to file charges against Morgan Grenfell for severe violation of the fund's obligations to declare their shareholdidng in listed companies. Norwegian securities regulations oblige shareholders to notify the bourse when they own 10, 25 and 50 percent of a company.

-Paper producer Norske Skog posted nine-month operating profits down 6.5 percent at 1.48 billion crowns compared with 1.59 billion crowns compared with a year-ago. Despite lower results the A share closed two crowns up to 179 crowns on Thursday.
-Over the past year the number of jobless has fallen by 74,000. However unemployment among women has increased. For the first time in eight years, unemployment is higher among women than men.
